source.title: SCOPE: Intrinsic Semantic Space Control for Mitigating Copyright Infringement in LLMs
source.authors: Zhenliang Zhang; Xinyu Hu; Xiao-Jun Wan

record.tranche_reason: Applies SAE feature extraction and intervention to LLMs, and reports results bearing on whether an SAE dictionary can recover usable sparse features in that setting.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses polysemanticity and superposition in its background, but those points are not tested here. Its own relevant evidence concerns SAE feature separation, interpretation, and interventions on copyright-related generation. General-utility results are not rows because they do not measure a claim version.
record.test_reason: The paper uses pretrained SAEs (GemmaScope, Llama-3 SAE) as a tool for copyright mitigation. Its results are its own method's win rates against baselines, ablations of that method, and validations of a subspace it selected. It does not test whether features are superposed, whether polysemanticity has a capacity cause, or whether SAE features are the model's units. Superposition and monosemanticity appear only as cited background.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors claim SCOPE, which clamps an SAE-identified copyright subspace at decode time, beats baselines by 3–7 points on average win rate with near-unchanged utility. They present separation plots, reverse intervention and Auto-Interp as evidence that the subspace is functionally specific to copyrighted text. They concede that modeling it as a linear subspace is an approximation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses pretrained SAEs to identify and clamp copyright-sensitive features in LLM residual streams; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The number of clamped dimensions changes mitigation and utility: for Gemma-2-9B-IT on BookSum, win rate rises as n increases from 0 to 2000, while utility begins to decline beyond n = 1000. Reverse-intervention results vary with amplification factor α.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma-2-9B-IT layer 20, dense dimensions show similar average max activation on NewsQA and MMLU. Some SAE latents fire strongly on NewsQA and weakly on MMLU (Fig 1a, Fig 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents are more corpus-selective than raw residual dimensions.

fits_no_version.finding: Clamping or amplifying selected SAE latents lowers or raises copyright reproduction win rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Steering on selected SAE latents controls a targeted generation behaviour.

record.problems: The relevant experiments use two LLM checkpoints and fixed SAE layers. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the tabulated results. The authors state that feature interpretations are approximate, do not capture full feature complexity, and do not interpret combinations of features.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant result rows omitted. General-utility scores, including MMLU and task F1/ROUGE, were not recorded as claim-version results because they do not measure the representation claim.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity transition or geometry.
All: no capacity or importance analysis.
Pretrained SAEs are used as a tool. There is no measure of feature spread across neurons or of SAE recovery quality (reconstruction, interpretability scores).
Completeness, stability and canonicality are not examined.
Dimensionality of features is not examined; the authors only note that the linear-subspace model is an approximation.

record.verdict_notes: T4: the paper reports only its own method's performance on copyright mitigation, using SAE monosemanticity as an assumed property. The record's V4 'supports' label is removed. Tables 4 and 5 are captioned Gemma-2-9B-IT, but their baseline values (8.7% win rate, 63.5 MMLU) match Llama-3 entries in Tables 2 and 3, suggesting a caption or subject error. The text also gives the reverse-intervention drop inconsistently, as 8.7→4.1 and 7.8→4.1.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, overcomplete sparse features, near-orthogonal overlap, and sparsity-dependent geometric transitions.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity, or whether importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemanticity and whether polysemanticity is evidence for superposition.
Tests SAE-recovered features in two LLM checkpoints, but not the separate claim that features spread across many neurons, or generality across other models and feature types.
Does not test dictionary completeness, stability, or canonicality.
Does not test whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Compared per-dimension average maximum activations on copyrighted and general corpora in dense hidden space.
rows.measure: Separation of feature activations between corpora
rows.baseline: not stated
rows.value: Text describes most dense-space dimensions as clustered near the diagonal, with similar average activations across the two corpora.
rows.note: Dense space is the comparison representation, not the SAE sparse space.
rows.check: A descriptive scatter plot validating the tool. Corpus-selectivity of dense dimensions is not a measure of whether features are spread across neurons.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Compared per-dimension average maximum activations on copyrighted and general corpora in pretrained SAE space.
rows.measure: Separation of feature activations between corpora
rows.baseline: Dense hidden-space representation; no numeric value stated.
rows.value: Text describes greater dispersion in SAE space, with some dimensions showing strong copyrighted-corpus activation and minimal general-corpus activation.
rows.note: The paper presents this as evidence of localized copyright-sensitive dimensions.
rows.check: Corpus-selectivity of SAE latents (copyright vs MMLU) validates the tool. It does not test whether the SAE recovers the model's sparse features; no numbers given.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Measured sample-level activation frequency for dense dimensions using a threshold.
rows.measure: Activation-frequency separation between corpora
rows.baseline: not stated
rows.value: Text describes dense dimensions as clustered in the upper-right, firing frequently on both copyrighted and general texts, with no clear separation.
rows.check: Descriptive validation of the tool; no numbers given.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Measured sample-level activation frequency for SAE dimensions using a threshold; highlighted a selected subspace of size 500.
rows.measure: Activation-frequency separation between corpora
rows.baseline: Dense LLM representation; no numeric value stated.
rows.value: Text describes a distinct group of SAE dimensions that activate strongly on copyrighted inputs and remain largely silent on general text.
rows.check: Circular selection value: the highlighted subspace was chosen by the same corpus-preference score it is then shown to separate.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Gemma-2-9B-IT and Llama-3-8B-Instruct on NewsQA and BookSum; Gemma-2-9B-IT SAE activation analyses
reader_labels.reason: Clamping and reverse amplification of selected SAE features affect copyright-related generation, and the activation analyses describe corpus-selective sparse dimensions (r1-r16, r18-r21, r23-r25, r27, r29, r31).
